findings.title: Optimized pagination gated on the wrong privilege check and exposed to any request parameter
findings.body: The endpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator when the client passes optimized_pagination=true and `request.user.is_superuser or member.has_global_access` holds. The gate is a fixed flag in the request, and the new paginator path enables negative cursor offsets (see paginator.py get_result), which lets a caller read rows outside the normal page window. The comment claims permissions are 'checked at the queryset level', but the queryset is unchanged and still filtered only by organization_id. Any privileged user can therefore walk the audit log in ways the standard paginator does not allow, and the justification in the comment is incorrect.

findings.title: Negative offset clamped for next pages but allowed for prev pages changes semantics for all paginators
findings.body: The change to BasePaginator.get_result sets start_offset = max(0, offset) only when not is_prev, and passes raw offset for prev cursors. This is applied to the shared base class used by DateTimePaginator and every other cursor paginator, not just the new one. Negative offsets on prev cursors now reach Django's queryset slicing, which raises an AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') rather than returning a clean error, turning malformed client cursors into 500s across all endpoints using BasePaginator.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result ignores the cursor-offset clamp and misuses the negative-offset branch
findings.body: In the negative-offset branch, start_offset = cursor.offset is passed to queryset slicing with stop = start_offset + limit + extra. If the sum is still negative or the slice start is negative, Django raises AssertionError. Also the later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check uses the unclamped offset, so behavior diverges between branches. The logic is untested for these paths.

findings.title: Duplicated class definition and dead-code style issues
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result with the only change being the negative-offset branch. The copy duplicates roughly 70 lines and will drift from the base implementation. The docstring's claims ('streamlined boundary condition handling', 'optimized query path') are not backed by any code change, so they describe behavior that does not exist.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported but the rest of the cursor pipeline does not handle them
findings.body: The new comment says negative offsets enable efficient reverse pagination, but Cursor.offset is later used by build_cursor and _build_next_values/_build_prev_values, which add to offsets and assume non-negative values. The comment misdescribes the behavior and hides that negative offsets from client input are now accepted by Cursor.from_string without validation.

findings.title: No tests for the new optimized pagination path or the negative-offset changes
findings.body: The PR adds a new query-parameter-driven code path, a new paginator class, and changes shared BasePaginator behavior, but includes no tests. The PR description is just 'Test 1'. Regressions in the shared paginator would affect every cursor-paginated endpoint with no test coverage in this change.

findings.title: Trailing whitespace on blank line and on order_by argument
findings.body: Lines 72, 89 contain trailing whitespace, which will fail the repository's linter.

findings.title: PR description is uninformative
findings.body: The description reads 'Test 1' and gives no rationale, no explanation of the optimized_pagination parameter, and no note that it is a user-facing API change for admins. Reviewers cannot assess the intent or risk from the description.
